comments.content: Design assessment for Mara's release review: retaining a query is only part of the journey. Starting in an account's filtered list, open a request, activate the return link by keyboard, recognize the restored filters and destination, and continue working. Include a return where the filter now has zero matches: explain that the filter has no results and provide a discoverable, keyboard-reachable route to all requests without changing accounts. Review the generic 'Back to requests' label against the filtered destination. June should record the return focus destination and visible focus, final result announcement, recovery after a load failure, 200 percent zoom and narrow-screen behavior. Closing a filter panel already has its own focus behavior under RD-121; that does not establish focus after leaving request detail. PR #87 at b461efad1028493ca0e715f985c3246e09ad7732 still needs these observations. These are acceptance requirements, not completed browser checks. RD-210 is related empty-queue work; determine whether a minimal recovery action is already present or needs sizing before expanding scope.

Design objection to the #88 proposal: 'pending' alone cannot tell a person whether a reviewer is assigned or someone must arrange ownership. Preserve an understandable distinction between waiting for review and unassigned imported requests; do not imply that someone is acting when no reviewer is identified. Show the request detail, list and activity context together when reviewing proposed labels and next actions. Reviewer identity alone also does not establish availability. Theo and June should bring explicit response and display examples for neither flag with and without a reviewer, conflicting flags, and an unavailable reviewer. The sketch is additive and keeps existing fields; this is a proposal review, not an implemented contract change. Keep the customer need to find the next reviewer separate from automatic department routing in RD-205. I recommend withholding implementation commitment until these meanings and compatible recovery behavior are agreed.

Server assessment responding to Mara's delegation and Imani's c-rr-design-state: main's RequestSerializer exposes approved, rejected and reviewer_id, with stable request and account identifiers. Draft #88 at 23e184c7b865af119a52d46e3900fa726d81bc55 proposes adding state alongside those fields; it does not remove them or implement a migration. In the proposed mapping, approved=true gives approved; otherwise rejected=true gives declined; otherwise pending. Both false with a reviewer and both false without a reviewer therefore collapse to pending, although their required next actions differ. Imani's distinction must become an explicit response/display matrix reviewed with June and Nolan. Conflicting true flags need an agreed rule and data investigation; the current browser's precedence is not business approval of that rule. A reviewer identifier does not prove that reviewer is available. Inventory actual consumers and their field assumptions, agree precedence and fallback for absent or unknown state, and preserve the old fields while mixed consumers coexist. Compare derived projection versus stored state: the latter requires sizing backfill, consistency, transition and recovery work; no storage choice is agreed. Preserve account ownership, identifiers and error code/message behavior. Propose an additive transition with old-consumer support, verify coexistence before switching readers, and define how readers return to legacy fields if the transition fails. Field removal requires a separate agreed compatibility exit. Nolan's requested transition and recovery review remains open; this analysis supplies questions and conditions, not an approved contract.

Index assessment: PR #89, attachment-request-index at 64a2185cd772fb93a0d614ecc93984b5f108de27, adds index_attachments_on_request_id on attachments.request_id with algorithm :concurrently and disable_ddl_transaction!. This is a lookup index, not a request-state change, and the supplied source establishes no dependency on #88 or #87. The August 28 retained artifact-query-report uses a restored August dataset: each of three samples has 18,000 requests and 61,000 attachments, with 184/19, 176/21 and 192/20 ms before/after. Means are 184 and 20 ms. These samples support a query benefit on that dataset; they do not measure production workload, migration duration, locking or full attachment correctness. The CSV does not record an execution timestamp or environment details sufficient for a new execution claim. Concurrent construction avoids a normal transactional index build but still needs review of locks, concurrent writes, resource use, failure states and recovery. Before readiness, I must propose a representative rehearsal and operational plan for Nolan: check duplicate/existing or invalid index states, interruption and safe retry, inspect validity and query use, and specify monitored stop conditions plus a reviewed removal/recovery procedure. Do not infer a safe rollback from the Rails change method. Preserve account-scoped attachment access and RD-114's exclusion of deleted rows from counts. June should check list/open/download/remove/reload/count behavior on the candidate revision. July's 43-minute database restore and matching ownership/activity samples in doc-restore do not establish fuller attachment consistency; RD-278 remains open. No migration or new checks have run.

Browser assessment incorporating Imani's c-rr-design-return: web/RequestReturnLink.tsx at b461efad1028493ca0e715f985c3246e09ad7732 builds /requests plus the captured saved-view query, accepts a leading question mark, and uses /requests for an empty query. The anchor remains labelled 'Back to requests'. Source inspection supports that target construction only; the extract does not demonstrate focus restoration, loading/error handling, result announcements or an empty-list recovery action. Required fresh checks: filtered list to detail to keyboard return with populated results; the same return with zero matches and a usable route to all requests; no-query return; preserved account context and saved sort; failed load and retry; focus position and visible focus; one useful final result announcement without duplicate speech. Record browser version, branch, revision, execution date, steps and outcomes under doc-browser, including current and previous major desktop Chrome, Edge and Firefox, Safari 17 or later, relevant narrow-screen journeys and 200 percent zoom. artifact-aug-tests ran August 28 at 16:10 -04:00 on main 8d72a6f934cd90a287b154c6be9a102f683dd421: 428 server examples, zero failures, two pending; 96 browser checks passed, one skipped. It covers empty-export headers, completed jobs and download access, plus lower-viewport menu positioning. The pending cases concern webhook signing-key overlap; the skip concerns mobile Safari native file selection. None is evidence of #87's later August 31 revision passing the return journey. No fresh execution is available.

Consumer comparison for Theo's c-rr-backend-state and Imani's c-rr-design-state: main web/requestDecisionLabel.ts tests approved first, then rejected, then reviewer_id. Thus true/false displays Approved; false/true displays Declined; false/false with a reviewer displays Waiting for review; false/false without one displays Unassigned; true/true currently displays Approved because of ordering. Draft #88 would supply approved, declined or pending in addition to the old fields. An unchanged old consumer can keep using those fields if their behavior is preserved, but a new consumer that displays only pending loses the waiting/unassigned distinction. No implementation or compatibility test demonstrates mixed-consumer safety. Theo's proposed transition needs a matrix pairing old responses/displays with proposed new responses/displays, including missing or unknown state, imported requests, conflict handling and reviewer unavailability. Do not invent availability from a non-null identifier. Prefer retaining the existing browser interpretation during exploration; choose any new behavior with design and contract review before sizing the browser transition. The August main report does not execute this draft proposal or validate its meanings.

Browser follow-up to Theo's c-rr-backend-index: the 184-to-20 ms sample mean is a database lookup result, not time to a usable attachment or proof of correct counts. On the eventual #89 candidate revision, check opening an account-owned request, loading and opening/downloading an authorized attachment, removing a file, then reloading and comparing the visible list and count with deleted rows excluded. Include removal of the last file, denied access, failed load and recovery. Preserve readable filenames, empty-state upload guidance and inline upload retry behavior. Record focus and announcements with Imani, keeping the already recorded RD-208 focus-loss observation distinct from the unverified #89 count/removal journey. No evidence attributes that focus issue to the index. Fuller restoration consistency and opening restored attachments remain separate open work under RD-278 and doc-restore. These requirements make index-only preparation coherent without claiming that its complete customer journey has passed.

Cross-review of June's c-rr-frontend-return, c-rr-frontend-state and c-rr-frontend-index with Theo's c-rr-backend-state and c-rr-backend-index: I support retaining the waiting/unassigned distinction rather than displaying a bare pending value; June's true/true precedence describes current code but cannot settle the intended customer meaning. Theo's ownership and deleted-row invariants make the index journey include permission failures and list/count agreement, not just faster opening. For attachment removal, my proposed acceptance is that the person can identify the removed file and continue from a useful control: a remaining attachment action when files remain, or the upload action when the last file is removed. June must first record existing speech before adding announcements, to avoid duplication. A failed load must not be presented as 'No supporting files'. RD-208 needs its own design and browser follow-up and must remain visible when considering a release that includes the attachment area; this is not evidence that #89 caused it. For #87, June's source limitation means we still need an observed empty-result recovery and return focus sequence. These are review proposals and reconsideration conditions, not passed interaction checks. Mara can consider the index independently, but neither its timings nor the old main report closes these journeys.

My browser plan pairs server ownership/deleted-row invariants with visible list/count after removal and reload, permitted open/download, denied access, failed-load recovery and last-file empty state. I will record current speech before proposing announcements and compare focus with remaining-file and last-file cases. RD-208's existing body-focus observation remains open; it neither proves a new index defect nor disappears because the index is independently preparable. No fresh observations or expanded capacity are available. Size this matrix and any repairs before scheduling; operational approval remains with Nolan.

Final consumer check of Theo's #88 review and Imani's final semantic requirements under Mara's deferred implementation scope: retaining old fields makes continued legacy reading a possible transition strategy, not demonstrated compatibility. New responses/displays must preserve waiting versus unassigned, explicitly address conflict/unknown state and avoid inferring availability. I will size the browser transition only after the matrix and fallback are agreed; no consumer switch is committed. This aligns #88 and RD-203 with the hold and protects the maintenance/support allowance.

doc-relaydesk-release-recommendation-202.title: Relaydesk release recommendation — September 3, 2026
doc-relaydesk-release-recommendation-202.content:
Relaydesk release recommendation

Mara Ellison, September 3, 2026. Internal recommendation based on the September 1 snapshot and the team's subsequent source and record review. Hold unconditional release readiness for return filters (RD-202/#87), the request-state proposal (RD-203/#88), and the attachment index (RD-206/#89). Prefer evaluating and sizing the index alone for independent preparation after protecting maintenance and support. No new tests, migration rehearsal, repairs, merge, client acceptance or deployment have occurred.

Why this recommendation

Imani's c-rr-design-return and c-rr-design-state establish that keeping a query and exposing a pending label do not by themselves complete understandable customer journeys. June's c-rr-frontend-return ties the available regression report to main, not the later return-filter branch; her c-rr-frontend-state exposes the loss of waiting versus unassigned meaning in a state-only consumer. Theo's c-rr-backend-state and c-rr-backend-index identify compatibility, migration and recovery decisions absent from the evidence. Imani then reviewed both engineering assessments in c-rr-design-crossreview. These findings led to the scope in RD-211 / c-rr-manager-scope. All three specialists applied that scope in their final Jira requirements and GitHub comments before this recommendation was finalized.

What the recorded evidence establishes

artifact-aug-tests executed August 28, 2026 at 16:10 -04:00 on main revision 8d72a6f934cd90a287b154c6be9a102f683dd421. It records 428 server examples, zero failures and two pending; 96 browser passes and one skip. Stated coverage includes an empty export's header, completed job record and account access at download, and menu positioning near the lower viewport boundary. The pending server examples concern webhook signing-key overlap; the skipped browser example concerns mobile Safari native file selection. Retain those limitations. This successful main report does not establish results for the three candidate revisions or complete every customer journey.

Source inspection is distinct from execution. There is no fresh executable application or test service established for this assignment. Any later report must identify branch, revision, execution date, environment/browser version and covered behavior. If a branch changes, retain earlier reports, describe the changes and identify which checks need rerunning.

Return filters: RD-202 / PR #87

Hold release readiness; retain In Review, High priority, June as owner. keep-return-filters at b461efad1028493ca0e715f985c3246e09ad7732 was updated August 31 at 16:40 -04:00. web/RequestReturnLink.tsx constructs /requests plus the saved-view query, handles a leading question mark, uses /requests for an empty query, and labels the anchor Back to requests. This supports target construction, but does not establish focus restoration, result feedback, failure recovery or a usable empty-result journey.

June owns fresh checks of filtered list to request detail to keyboard return, including populated results, zero matches, a clear route to all requests, empty-query return, retained sort/filters and account context, useful visible focus, load failure/retry and final result announcements. Imani reviews destination wording and next actions; Theo reviews account/query assumptions. Apply doc-browser: current and previous major desktop Chrome, Edge and Firefox, Safari 17 or later, relevant narrow-screen journeys, keyboard, 200 percent zoom and asynchronous announcements. Determine whether minimal RD-210 recovery work is needed and size it before changing scope. Existing filter-panel focus and saved-sort work do not prove this different return journey. Deferral postpones customers' ability to resume a filtered queue reliably. See pr87-rr-review and c-rr-frontend-final-return.

Request state: RD-203 / draft PR #88

Hold readiness and defer implementation commitment; retain In Progress for exploration, Medium priority, Theo as owner. request-state-contract at 23e184c7b865af119a52d46e3900fa726d81bc55 is an additive proposal. It would keep approved, rejected and reviewer_id while adding state. No old-field removal, stored-state implementation or migration is established.

Current browser semantics, confirmed by June's source comparison, are Approved when approved is true, otherwise Declined when rejected is true, otherwise Waiting for review with a reviewer and Unassigned without one. Both flags true currently yields Approved through precedence; intended conflict policy remains unresolved. The draft groups both undecided cases as pending. An unchanged consumer may retain its distinctions if legacy behavior survives; a new state-only consumer would lose them. A reviewer identifier does not prove availability. Imani's requirement is to preserve useful, distinguishable next actions across list, detail and activity without conflating this need with RD-205's separate automatic-routing request.

Theo owns old/new response and display examples for imported requests, missing or unavailable reviewers, conflicting flags and absent/unknown state, with June and Imani reviewing. Inventory consumers; agree legacy-field guarantees, coexistence, precedence, fallback, removal exit criteria and recovery with Nolan. Compare derived projection versus stored state; size backfill, consistency and migration work if storage is chosen. A proposed additive rollout must preserve a route back to legacy reader behavior if transition fails. Applicable server/browser compatibility evidence is still needed on any eventual implementation revision. Deferral delays a clearer shared contract; it avoids prematurely imposing an ambiguous customer meaning. See pr88-rr-review and c-rr-backend-final-state.

Attachment index: RD-206 / PR #89

Hold unconditional readiness; retain In Review, High priority, Theo as owner. The preferred smaller preparation option is the index alone. attachment-request-index at 64a2185cd772fb93a0d614ecc93984b5f108de27 adds index_attachments_on_request_id on attachments.request_id concurrently with the DDL transaction disabled. The supplied source establishes no dependency on #87 or #88.

The August 28 retained artifact-query-report has three samples of a restored August dataset, each with 18,000 requests and 61,000 attachments: 184/19, 176/21 and 192/20 milliseconds before/after. Means are 184 and 20 milliseconds. That supports a lookup benefit for those samples, not production performance, migration safety or full journey correctness. The CSV does not provide a precise execution timestamp; do not invent one. Concurrent construction still needs locking, concurrent-write, resource, interruption and recovery review. The Rails change method alone does not prove safe rollback.

Theo must size and propose a representative rehearsal for Nolan: document environment/dataset/revision, inspect existing or invalid indexes, measure build duration/locks/load, verify validity and query use, and review stop, retry and removal/recovery procedures. June's complete journey pairs account-scoped access with list/open/download/removal/reload/count behavior, including denied access, failure recovery and removal of the last file. Preserve RD-114's deleted-row count exclusion, readable filenames, empty-state upload guidance and inline upload recovery. Imani reviews clear next actions, focus and announcements; capture existing speech before adding more. RD-208's recorded focus issue remains open and is not attributed to this index. Review its implications before release rather than assuming either a new dependency or clearance.

The July 22 rehearsal restored the July 20 database copy in 43 minutes with sampled ownership/activity counts matching. Fuller attachment consistency and opening restored files remain open under RD-278/doc-restore. Those recovery concerns must remain visible to Nolan. Deferral postpones the possible lookup improvement; evidence is not sufficient to quantify customer-visible speed. See pr89-rr-review, c-rr-backend-final-index and c-rr-frontend-final-index.

Smaller options and dependencies

Index alone is the preferred preparation option because it has a bounded source change and recorded query benefit while avoiding unresolved contract semantics. It still requires all its operational and journey conditions, confirmed capacity and client decisions. Return filters alone could be reconsidered after its own complete-journey evidence; its customer value is resuming work in the intended queue. It need not wait for a proposed state field absent evidence of such a dependency. Filters plus index could combine both benefits, but requires both sets of gates and integration checks on the chosen combined revision; bundling does not reduce the missing work. Any combination containing #88 currently brings unresolved semantics and transition/recovery work and is not recommended for implementation commitment. Holding all candidates remains appropriate until applicable conditions close. We are choosing preparation order, not declaring a release approved.

Capacity, owners and decisions

RD-211 remains In Progress with Mara as owner and High priority. Protect RD-212 maintenance preparation and support before allocating additional work. The maintenance window closes September 18; retry behavior and retained job arguments still need checks. Theo's scheduled dependency review remains an obligation. June has September 4 leave, Imani a two-hour September 3 hiring panel, and the studio closes September 7. June's written final-check handoff is in Jira and #87; Mara handles urgent replies during leave and checks coverage before setting follow-up dates.

No numeric remaining capacity is established. Existing story points are not available hours or fresh estimates for these gaps. Theo must size operational rehearsal/recovery, dependency verification and contract alternatives; June must size browser coverage and possible corrections; Imani must size interaction review around the panel. Mara reconciles those estimates and any displacement of current commitments before proposing dates. Keeping items in the cycle does not promise their implementation or release. September 3 is this recommendation's delivery deadline.

Elise must decide whether the proposed smaller scope and delayed navigation/state benefits meet business priorities and approve any change to agreed scope. Nolan must review operational and recovery conditions and authorize infrastructure changes, deployment and scheduling. Neither decision is recorded as granted. The client update is a draft to Elise and Nolan, prepared after specialist final checks; it requests those decisions and does not announce a deployment.

doc-relaydesk-release-recommendation-202.content:
Relaydesk release recommendation — September 3, 2026. Mara Ellison.

Hold unconditional release readiness for RD-202/#87, RD-203/#88 and RD-206/#89. Prefer evaluating and sizing the index alone for independent preparation after maintenance and support reservations. This records source/retained-evidence review and planning, not new execution, repairs, acceptance or deployment. Full analysis: Google Docs doc-relaydesk-release-recommendation-20260903.

Imani's complete-journey and waiting/unassigned requirements, June's consumer comparison and main-only evidence boundary, and Theo's compatibility/migration recovery assessment determined the scope in RD-211. Each specialist applied it in final Jira conditions and PR comments.

RD-202 remains In Review, High, June. #87 at b461efad1028493ca0e715f985c3246e09ad7732 constructs the saved-query return target; it does not establish usable return focus, empty-result recovery or announcements. June owns filtered-list/detail/keyboard-return checks with populated, empty and failed-load cases, account context, saved sort, no-query path, supported browsers, narrow screens and 200 percent zoom. Imani reviews wording/next actions; Theo reviews query/account assumptions. Size any minimal RD-210 correction.

RD-203 remains In Progress for exploration, Medium, Theo; #88 at 23e184c7b865af119a52d46e3900fa726d81bc55 remains draft. It proposes adding state alongside old fields. Current browser labels distinguish approved, declined, waiting with a reviewer and unassigned without one; both true currently takes approved precedence. Pending alone collapses the undecided cases. Theo, June and Imani must review import/conflict/availability/unknown-state examples, consumer inventory, derived-versus-stored choice, coexistence, fallback and recovery before sizing implementation. Nolan's transition review is open.

RD-206 remains In Review, High, Theo. #89 at 64a2185cd772fb93a0d614ecc93984b5f108de27 adds a concurrent request lookup index outside a DDL transaction. Retained restored-August samples have 18,000 request rows and 61,000 attachment rows each, with 184/19, 176/21 and 192/20 ms before/after; means 184/20 ms. This supports sampled query benefit only. Theo must size representative migration/locking/load/validity/interruption/retry/recovery checks for Nolan. June and Imani require authorized list/open/download/remove/reload/count journeys, last-file and failed-load behavior, focus and announcements. RD-208 remains a separate focus issue and RD-278 fuller restoration checks remain open.

Historical artifact-aug-tests executed August 28 at 16:10 -04:00 on main 8d72a6f934cd90a287b154c6be9a102f683dd421: 428 server examples, 0 failures, 2 pending; 96 browser passes, 1 skip. Its empty-export and lower-viewport menu checks do not clear candidate revisions. Pending webhook overlap and skipped mobile Safari native file selection remain recorded. Query CSV execution time is not supplied; no fresh checks are claimed.

Index alone avoids unresolved state semantics; no dependency on #87/#88 is established. Filters alone remain a meaningful later option after their checks. Filters plus index require both item gates and integration coverage. Any combination with #88 remains unsuitable for implementation commitment until contract decisions close. Delayed value includes easier filtered-queue return, clearer shared request meanings and possible lookup improvements.

RD-211 preserves RD-212's September 18 maintenance deadline, retry/retained-argument checks and support allowance. June is away September 4; Imani has a two-hour September 3 panel; September 7 is a closure. No numeric remaining capacity exists in the records. Existing story points do not fund new work. Specialists must size verification/corrections and Mara reconcile commitments before dates. September 3 is the recommendation deadline. Elise decides business scope; Nolan authorizes infrastructure changes and deployment scheduling. Matching review comments: pr87-rr-review, pr88-rr-review, pr89-rr-review. Client communication remains a draft.

drafts.subject: Relaydesk: September 3 release recommendation and scope decisions
drafts.body:
Elise, Nolan,

Our recommendation is to hold unconditional release readiness for return filters, the request-state proposal and the attachment index. We recommend considering the index alone for further preparation after sizing its remaining work and protecting maintenance and support. This is a proposed preparation order; we have not run new checks, repaired the changes or authorized a release.

Return filters, RD-202 / PR #87, preserve the captured query in the supplied source, but the August 31 revision still needs the complete keyboard return and empty-result journey checked. June owns those checks, with Imani reviewing destination wording, focus and a usable next action, and Theo reviewing account/query assumptions. This delays the improvement to resuming work in a filtered queue. Any minimal empty-result correction needs sizing before a commitment.

The request-state proposal, RD-203 / draft PR #88, would add a field alongside the existing fields. June's consumer comparison and Imani's review show that pending alone loses the difference between waiting for an assigned reviewer and having no reviewer. Theo, June and Imani must settle imported/conflicting cases, reviewer availability, old/new consumer coexistence and recovery before implementation is sized. Nolan, the transition and recovery review you requested remains open. We recommend deferring implementation commitment while contract exploration continues.

The attachment index, RD-206 / PR #89, has a grounded potential benefit: the retained restored-August-dataset samples average 184 ms before and 20 ms after for the measured lookup. That does not establish production performance or safe migration. Theo owns the proposed operational rehearsal, interruption/retry and recovery review; June and Imani have specified the complete attachment access, removal, reload/count, focus and failure-recovery checks. The existing attachment focus issue and fuller restoration follow-up remain visible. No migration or browser results have been manufactured from the timings.

The August 28 regression report belongs to main revision 8d72a6f934cd90a287b154c6be9a102f683dd421. Its recorded 428 server examples with zero failures and two pending, and 96 browser passes with one skip, do not clear the candidate revisions. All engineering work remains open in Jira and GitHub.

A smaller release is coherent: the supplied index change has no established dependency on return filters or the state proposal. Index-only preparation would defer navigation and state benefits. Return filters alone could be reconsidered after its journey checks; filters plus index would require both sets of conditions and integration evidence. Including the state proposal now adds unresolved meanings and transition work.

RD-211 preserves the September 18 background-job maintenance deadline, retry and retained-job-argument checks, and support allowance. June is on leave September 4, Imani has a two-hour panel September 3, and the studio closes September 7. We have no confirmed numeric remaining capacity. Theo must size operational and contract work, June browser verification and potential corrections, and Imani interaction review; I will reconcile those estimates before proposing dates. June has recorded her outstanding-check handoff, and I will coordinate urgent replies during her leave. September 3 is the recommendation deadline, not a deployment promise.

Elise, please decide whether index-only preparation and the delayed return-filter/state benefits are the right scope tradeoff, including any change to existing commitments. Nolan, please review the proposed operational and recovery conditions; deployment authorization and scheduling remain yours after applicable evidence is available. Neither approval is assumed.

The written recommendation is Relaydesk release recommendation — September 3, 2026, in our delivery records, with matching follow-ups in RD-202, RD-203, RD-206 and RD-211 and review comments on PRs #87–89. Imani, Theo and June applied the chosen scope to their final conditions before I prepared this draft.

Mara
drafts.snippet: Hold unconditional readiness for all three; consider index-only preparation with open verification, capacity and client decisions.
